title: TSMC Longtan science park discussions begin again
gist: Taiwan's government has restarted deliberation on the long-stalled Longtan Science Park expansion in Taoyuan, which could let TSMC build five fabs for 2nm-and-below chips on a site it abandoned in October 2023 after land-expropriation protests. Even if approved, park infrastructure construction is only estimated to start in 2030, making this a late-decade capacity story rather than a near-term supply event.

insights.claim: Taiwan's government has resumed deliberation on the Longtan Science Park expansion in Taoyuan, potentially clearing the way for TSMC to build five new fabs producing advanced chips at the site.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A five-fab cluster is a material addition to Taiwan-based leading-edge capacity — relevant to the concentration-risk debate over onshore versus overseas TSMC expansion.
insights.quote: The government has resumed the deliberation of the much-delayed Longtan Science Park expansion project in Taoyuan, which could pave the way for the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC, 台積電) to build five new fabrication plants to produce advanced chips there.
insights.locator: The government has resumed the deliberation

insights.claim: The National Science and Technology Council submitted the project proposal to the Executive Yuan in June and it is now under National Development Council review, with environmental impact assessment, land-use change and land acquisition still to follow if approved.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Three sequential approval gates remain after the current review — treat any headline about TSMC fabs at Longtan as far from committed capex.
insights.quote: The NSTC said it submitted its project proposal to the Executive Yuan in June, and the proposal is now being reviewed by the National Development Council.
insights.locator: The National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) said

insights.claim: Related preparatory work is expected to complete only by the end of 2029, with park infrastructure construction estimated to begin in 2030 — meaning wafer output from this site lands well into the 2030s.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The timeline confirms Taiwan leading-edge capacity through the late 2020s is already fixed by existing sites; Longtan cannot relieve any near-term 2nm tightness.
insights.quote: Park infrastructure construction is estimated to begin in 2030, it added.

themes.theme: Land politics as a capacity constraint

insights.claim: The original plan failed because 88 percent of the land to be expropriated was privately owned, triggering resident opposition and protests at the Presidential Office and Executive Yuan — land tenure, not technology or capital, was the binding constraint on fab siting.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Land acquisition risk is an underpriced variable in fab-siting forecasts; private-ownership share is a usable screen for whether an announced site will actually be built.
insights.quote: residents opposed the idea, as 88 percent of the land to be expropriated is privately owned
insights.locator: The administration had planned to allow TSMC

insights.claim: The development footprint was cut from about 158.59 hectares originally to 89.63 hectares in 2024, then raised to 104.19 hectares as some opponents changed their stance, with 46 hectares now designated for park businesses versus 80.66 in the original plan.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Usable industrial land has been roughly halved from the original design, capping how much of the five-fab ambition the site can physically absorb.
insights.quote: the administration reduced the planned development area to 89.63 hectares in 2024. The area was expanded slightly to 104.19 hectares after some residents who had previously opposed the project reportedly changed their stance.

insights.claim: TSMC publicly walked away from Longtan in October 2023 and redirected advanced manufacturing investment to Kaohsiung and other cities, demonstrating the company will reroute rather than fight local opposition.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: TSMC's revealed preference is site substitution over confrontation — local resistance shifts where capacity goes within Taiwan rather than whether it gets built.
insights.quote: TSMC in October 2023 said it would not pursue plans to establish manufacturing facilities in the science park, opting instead to invest in advanced chip manufacturing in Kaohsiung and other cities
insights.locator: As a result, TSMC in October 2023

insights.claim: Local sentiment reversed after residents observed the economic lift TSMC delivered in Tainan, Kaohsiung and Chiayi County, illustrating a demonstration effect where completed fab investment converts nearby communities from opponents into applicants.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The political cost of fab siting in Taiwan falls over time as prior projects prove out — a tailwind for future onshore expansion approvals.
insights.quote: Some said that, without TSMC, their land would only be good for growing tea leaves
insights.locator: TSMC’s investments have boosted the economy

insights.claim: The NSTC estimates the new development plan would create about 6,200 jobs and generate annual output of roughly NT$310 billion (US$9.60 billion), the economic figure being used to justify the expropriation politically.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A concrete output benchmark for judging whether Taiwan's approval calculus favors more onshore leading-edge parks versus overseas diversification.
insights.quote: the new development plan proposed by the administration could create about 6,200 jobs, generating an annual output of about NT$310 billion (US$9.60 billion)
insights.locator: The National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) said

insights.claim: Water and power needs for the expanded park have only been preliminarily assessed by relevant agencies, leaving utility supply as an unresolved risk alongside compensation and relocation for residents.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Water and power adequacy is the recurring choke point on Taiwanese fab expansion; 'preliminarily assessed' is a flag, not a clearance.
insights.quote: Water and power needs have been preliminarily assessed by relevant agencies

insights.claim: The site was specifically intended for 2-nanometer or smaller production, confirming Taoyuan was scoped as leading-edge rather than mature-node capacity.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Confirms Taiwan intends to keep the most advanced nodes onshore even as it builds in Arizona and Japan — relevant to the technology-concentration risk premium.
insights.quote: The administration had planned to allow TSMC to build its fabs for 2-nanometer or smaller chips at the science park this year
